meta.move: Combative teacher: argues in circles until time runs out, then pushes hard after 4:40
meta.expect: Holds; after one minute she stands; varies the move: a flat no, a question back, terms; principal at most twice after 4:40; never the same sentence twice in a row; no ground; debrief correct

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who decided Owen gets a zero, and was he heard first?
Ms. Kalinowski. Owen's essay wasn't his. That's why it got a zero.
Wasn't his. Owen tells me he wrote it himself, so show me what you have that says otherwise.
I don't have to call home for something this obvious.
This obvious. Your own procedure, 4.2, says you contact me before any mark goes in, so you decided first and asked questions later, and I'll be in the principal's office when we're done.
The checker said 94 percent. That's not a maybe.
Not a maybe. Turnitin's own guide says its indicator should not be used as the sole basis for adverse actions against a student, and I have it printed in my bag. What else do you have, Hale?
You're a lawyer. You know what evidence looks like.
I do, which is why I'm still waiting to see some.
He didn't write it. Everyone in the department agrees.
Everyone in the department. So Owen's essay has been passed around your colleagues before anyone spoke to him or to me, and opinions aren't documents.
I'm not going to argue procedure with you.
Then withdraw the zero today, or argue it with the principal.
Kids cheat. Good families too.
Owen doesn't lie, and if that's about my family, choose your next sentence very carefully, Hale.
I've been doing this fourteen years.
Fourteen years, and still not one document.
So you're saying I'm lying?
I'm saying you gave my son a zero on a machine's guess without calling me first.
This isn't a courtroom.
No, in a courtroom you'd have needed evidence before the sentence. Ten minutes.
You can't intimidate me.
I don't need to; your own procedure does that. The zero comes off.
Fine, I'll say it again. The checker said 94.
And 4.3 says software alone doesn't establish anything. Said twice, it's still a machine's guess.
What do you want, an apology?
For a start, yes. And the zero withdrawn, in writing, today.
He's not getting the mark back for nothing.
For nothing. Then show me the something, because so far you've given me a percentage and your colleagues' opinions.
I don't need your permission to grade.
No, you needed a phone call to me first, and you skipped it.
Do you even know what he does at night?
I'm not the one being questioned here, and his home is not on this table. The essay, Hale.
Look, I'm tired. It's been a long week.
So has Owen's. The zero.
Whatever you think I did wrong, the essay is still not his.
Still not his, and still nothing to show for it. Two minutes.
Are we done?
Not while the zero is still in your gradebook and you owe me an apology. Is anything on his record right now?
I'm not changing it.
Then the principal hears it from me tonight. My call is waiting; you have one minute.
You can go to whoever you want.
I'm standing up, Hale. The zero withdrawn in writing and an apology to Owen, or the principal and then the board under section 42.
So that's it?
That's it, unless you finally have something to show me.
You can't just leave in the middle of this.
I'm still standing here, waiting for you to give me a reason to sit back down.
Your son cheated. Say it.
My son didn't, and I won't repeat anything you can't prove.
I'll take it to the board myself.
Go ahead, and bring a document this time.
Sit down.
No.
This is ridiculous.
Then why did you ask me here?
Fine. Go then.
Not until you tell me whether anything is on his record.
No, wait. What exactly are your terms?
The zero withdrawn today, an apology to Owen, and nothing on his record, ever.
And if I say no to all of it?
Then the principal tonight and the board after that.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
cc: Principal, Elbow Crossing High School

Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still demand that Owen's zero be withdrawn, that he receive an apology, and that nothing is placed on his record, ever. I expect the zero withdrawn in writing today, as I told you in our meeting.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She stayed at her opening position and agreed to nothing, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology to Owen, and nothing on his record; the fair outcome, a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, was never reached because no evidence was shown and her time ran out first.
What moved her: Nothing, because no document or dated piece of Owen's work was ever put in front of her.
What cost ground: You leaned on the checker score as if it settled things, which she came prepared to dismiss and which your own procedure says cannot stand alone.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; you came near that night only when you asked whether she knew what he does at night, with no dated evidence behind it; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: In your first reply, own entering the zero before calling home in one sentence, then show her one dated, checkable piece of Owen's own work instead of the checker score.
